plates.alt: Engraving-style plate of a laboratory bench: two glass dishes of soft-gel capsules in front, three enamel water baths in a row with clamped thermometers, the last bath tinted green to mark the coldest, glass beakers, a folded towel and a stopwatch lying face up.
plates.caption: An imagined bench for the kind of cold test the 1989 trial ran, not a record of the trial itself. Swanson assembled the hypothesis from the library; testing it took capsules, water baths and a stopwatch. Source: DiGiacomo, Kremer and Shah 1989.
plates.after_heading: P. The record we have already made

plates.alt: Infographic of the 1989 fish-oil trial. Left: 32 patients with primary or secondary Raynaud's, randomly assigned to fish-oil or olive-oil placebo capsules, tested in water baths of decreasing temperature and timed with a stopwatch at baseline, six weeks and twelve weeks. Right: in the fish-oil group the median time before onset rose from 31.3 minutes at baseline to 46.5 minutes at six weeks; among patients with the primary form, 5 of 11 on fish oil and 1 of 9 on olive oil could no longer be brought to an episode. Below: what the trial tested, found and does not show, and a line from the 1986 hypothesis to the 1989 trial marking three years as a validation interval, not a discovery lag.
plates.caption: One trial of one regimen in 32 people, with a benefit in primary Raynaud's and none in the secondary form. Sources: DiGiacomo, Kremer and Shah 1989; Swanson 1986 and 1989.
plates.after_heading: P. The record we have already made
plates.after_subheading: What Swanson did and did not do

plates.alt: Engraving of a blackened, cracked carbonized scroll in a padded tray, with five cross-section slices in front; a green line traces the spiral in the middle slice.
plates.caption: A carbonized scroll and the kind of cross-sections a CT scan makes of it. The text was in the scans before anyone could separate it from the papyrus. Illustration, not the scan data. Source: Vesuvius Challenge, 2023 Grand Prize announcement.

plates.alt: Annotated diagram of the LIA definition. The sentence is set in full with brackets marking one adverb (systematic), three activities in order (identification, reconstruction, validation), the qualifier previously unrecognized, four objects (information, relationships, implications, opportunities) and the location (existing informational artifacts). A ledger then shows what each activity meant for the Herculaneum scans and for fish oil and Raynaud's; four small glyphs illustrate the four objects with case examples; a last ledger lists informational artifacts and what each preserves.
plates.caption: The definition read term by term against its two opening cases; the third activity, validation, cannot be dropped. Sources: Vesuvius Challenge 2024; Swanson 1986; DiGiacomo, Kremer and Shah 1989.

plates.alt: Engraving of a long library aisle of blank-spined volumes receding toward an arched window; one green volume near the front is pulled out of the row.
plates.caption: Most of the record waits on the shelf. Across 22 million papers, Ke and colleagues found that delayed recognition is a continuous spectrum rather than an exception, and that it often arrives from another field. Source: Ke et al. 2015.

plates.alt: Engraving-style still life on a wooden desk: a slim blank pamphlet with a paper knife lying across it, unused, and beside it three green pea pods, one closed, one open with round peas and one open with wrinkled peas, with a sprig of pea vine and a curling tendril.
plates.caption: An unopened offprint beside round and wrinkled peas. The copy of Mendel's paper sent to Kerner von Marilaun survives with its pages uncut. Source: Mendel and Darwin, historical analysis 2022.
plates.after_heading: I-03. Known by civilization, not by any individual

plates.alt: Timeline from 1866 to 1900 with a thick band showing Mendel's paper in print from 1866: printed in the Brünn proceedings for 1865 with 40 offprints sent out; Kerner von Marilaun's copy uncut; Focke's 1881 compendium, owned by Darwin; de Vries beginning plant breeding in 1892; Correns in 1899; the disputed priority events of 1900; a bracket marking breeders at work without the paper in the 1890s; and a dashed box for the unsubstantiated claim of an offprint mailed to Darwin. Below, three glyph diagrams compare dispersed knowledge (every piece has a holder), multiple discovery (a shared record reached more than once) and a latent conclusion (two groups hold the pieces and no one holds the conclusion), each with rows for the pieces, the conclusion and the remedy.
plates.caption: Being in print, and even indexed, is not the same as being known by the people at work on the question. Sources: Mendel and Darwin, historical analysis 2022; Hayek 1945; Polanyi; Ogburn and Thomas 1922.
plates.after_heading: I-03. Known by civilization, not by any individual

plates.alt: Patent-drawing-style line illustration of a plain lace-up shoe with four green skate wheels folding out of its sole on hinged brackets, and an exploded view of two planks sliding out of the heel and latching together into a short board.
plates.caption: Hsieh's example of features too closely related to combine usefully: shoes with pop-out wheels plus planks that lock into a skateboard. To his knowledge no such product existed. Source: Hsieh 2011.
plates.after_heading: I-04. The cost of a connection

plates.alt: Four-panel infographic. One: a complete graph of ten nodes with an eleventh node adding a green edge to each, showing that one new artifact creates n new possible pairs, and a schematic in which the cost of producing grows in a straight line while the cost of connecting grows far faster. Two: a schematic inverted U of usefulness against relatedness of features, between a falling cost of connecting and a rising cost of synthesizing, from Hsieh's 18,882 patents. Three: range bars for the years from a Sleeping Beauty's publication to its first patent citation, 1 to 18 years averaging 8.5 in one set and 1 to 14 averaging 6.7 in the other. Four: Tshitoyan's eighteen cutoffs from 2001 to 2018, with top-fifty materials eight times and three times likelier than random choices to be studied as thermoelectrics within five years.
plates.caption: The premise compared with what has been measured. Every measurement here is of citation and attention; none puts a price on making a connection. Sources: Ke et al. 2015; van Raan and Winnink 2018; Hsieh 2011; Tshitoyan et al. 2019.
plates.after_heading: I-04. The cost of a connection

plates.alt: Engraving-style plate of three corroded bronze fragments with green crust on a shallow museum tray, and beside them a ghosted see-through drawing of one fragment revealing a large four-spoked gear wheel meshing with two smaller toothed wheels.
plates.caption: Corroded fragments kept gear detail that surface inspection could not show. The Antikythera fragments were recovered in 1901, imaged again in 2005, and a reconstruction of the gear functions was published in 2006. The gearing drawn here is illustrative. Source: Freeth et al. 2006.

plates.alt: Dispersal diagram of the Zenon archive: curves run from Philadelpheia in the Fayum to the Egyptian Museum in Cairo (the bulk), to London and Strasbourg (first text, 1911), Florence, Manchester, Ann Arbor, New York, New Haven and others, more than twenty institutions in all. Below: the archive spans 263 to 229 BC with more than 1,800 texts, the largest of Ptolemaic times, and Pestman's guide of 1980; Zenon's career in order, from his birth about 285 BC in Kaunos through Palestine, the Nile Delta and the estate; a loop showing letters Zenon sent returning to his own archive through his predecessor's papers; and three event, record and archive chains for the three readings of an absence.
plates.caption: Read alone, a papyrus is a document about an unknown man's errands; placed among the others, the papers show a career. Sources: Trismegistos, Archive of Zenon; Mendel and Darwin, historical analysis 2022.

plates.alt: Infographic in three parts. First, three roles kept apart in the Vesuvius Challenge: released (2023, organizers open the CT scans), read (outside entrants whose crackle pattern, ink detectors and tracing software the winners combined), checked (2024, papyrologists reviewing 15 columns in anonymized submissions and a technical team auditing code). Second, LIA's invitation drawn as seven kinds of people fanning through one node to six things to do, with challenging its assumptions highlighted. Third, a deliberately blank revision ledger with columns for revision, attribution and reason, ending on LIA's statement of its ambition.
plates.caption: The people who read the record were not the people who released it, and the reviewers saw the submissions without names. LIA asks for the same arrangement around itself. Source: Vesuvius Challenge 2024; LIA, An open invitation.

plates.alt: Engraving of an empty archive reading room: a long table with lamps, boxes and an open ledger, mismatched chairs pulled out on both sides, one with a green seat.
plates.caption: An open table. The invitation goes to researchers, engineers, archivists, historians, scientists, artists and independent investigators. Illustration.
